tasks.name: Neuron Growth Simulation
tasks.systemPrompt:
Create a single self-contained HTML file using HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, and dat.gui.

Requirements:
- Use one 800×800 <canvas> centered on a dark background.
- Allowed external library: dat.gui for parameter controls.
- No other external libraries, frameworks, modules, or assets.
- Everything must be inside a single HTML file.

Color style:
- Use this exact neon palette:
  - Background: #05070f
  - Background glow: #101a3a
  - Main branch color: #00e5ff
  - Secondary branch accent: #d6ff00
  - Synapse color: #ff2bd6
  - Pulse color: #fff36a
  - UI/accent color: #ffd400
  - Optional dark grid/scanline color: rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.08)
- The final look should be futuristic, high contrast, glowing, and slightly gritty.
- Use canvas shadowBlur for neon glow effects.
- Do not use images or textures.
- Do not mention any game, movie, brand, or copyrighted visual style in the generated code or comments.

GUI:
- Add a dat.gui control panel.
- Organize controls into folders:
  - Growth
  - Synapses
  - Pulses
  - Visuals
- Include controls for:
  - neuron count
  - branch growth speed
  - max branch depth
  - branch split chance
  - branch curvature
  - max branch length
  - synapse distance threshold
  - synapse glow strength
  - pulse speed
  - pulse frequency
  - pulse brightness
  - background color
  - branch color
  - accent branch color
  - synapse color
  - pulse color
- Add buttons:
  - regenerate network
  - clear canvas
  - pause/resume animation

Simulation:
- Generate 3–6 random seed neurons near the center.
- Each neuron recursively grows branching axon/dendrite lines.
- Growth should be animated step-by-step, not instant.
- Branches move in slightly random directions with smooth organic curves.
- Use quadratic curves or lightweight smoothing for organic shapes.
- Randomly vary branch thickness slightly.
- Occasionally generate smaller side branches.
- Limit recursion depth and total branch count to keep performance stable.
- Use simple lightweight logic suitable for small LLM-generated code.

Connections:
- When two branch tips come within a small distance threshold, create a synapse.
- Prevent duplicate synapses between the same nearby branches.
- Synapses should glow softly and pulse over time.
- Animate a short electric pulse traveling between connected neurons.
- Pulses should move smoothly using interpolation.
- Store the network using lightweight arrays/objects only.

After generation:
- Stop growing once the network reaches a stable size.
- Continuously animate random electrical pulses traveling through existing connections.
- Randomly activate different paths over time.
- Keep the scene alive even after growth ends.

Visual effects:
- Draw thin glowing neon branches.
- Synapses should glow brighter than branches.
- Pulses should appear as moving electric sparks.
- Add subtle bloom using shadowBlur only.
- Add a faint vignette effect around the canvas edges.
- Optionally add lightweight scanlines or subtle animated background noise using canvas only.
- Maintain smooth animation with requestAnimationFrame.

Performance:
- Keep rendering lightweight.
- Avoid expensive particle systems.
- Avoid heavy physics or pathfinding.
- Target stable real-time animation in browser.

Code structure:
- Keep the code simple and compact.
- Separate logic into:
  - setup
  - GUI setup
  - neuron growth
  - synapse detection
  - pulse animation
  - rendering
- Add short comments explaining major sections.

Output:
- Save the implementation to the file "neuron_growth_{{MODEL_ID}}_01.html"

extraCriteria.name: Neural Network Growth
extraCriteria.description: Animated visualization of recursively growing neurons with glowing synaptic connections and traveling electrical pulses. The simulation renders a dynamic branching neural structure with configurable real-time parameters and neon visual effects.

extraCriteria.name: Functional GUI Controls
extraCriteria.description: The simulation must include a working dat.gui panel where parameter changes immediately affect the running visualization in real time.
